---
title: "Thesis timeline"
subtitle: "A notional five-quarter plan, with deliverables by quarter"
---

The timeline below is a notional plan for completing an NPS MS thesis in the Field
Robotics Lab.

::: {.callout-important}
To do a high-quality thesis requires that you commit to doing a thesis in FRL
**five quarters prior to your graduation**.
:::

## Generic thesis outline

For the purposes of this discussion, an NPS MS thesis consists of these chapters.
This is an approximation, not a rule.

1. **Introduction** — motivation, problem statement, contributions.
2. **Literature Review** — background, closely related work.
3. **Approach** — background, procedures, methods, models, experimental setup.
4. **Results and Analysis** — the majority of the technical contribution.
5. **Conclusion** — discussion, summary referring back to the problem statement and
   contributions, and future work.

## Time commitment

Thesis research in FRL takes more time than the four thesis blocks allocated in
your course matrix. The table below estimates the commitment in units of class
blocks — roughly double the time formally allocated.

| Quarter | 4 | 3 | 2 | 1 | 0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Description** | Background — problem statement, lit review, proposal | Foundation — tools, skills, prototyping | Execution — development, experiment | Documentation — document, draft | Graduation — administration, revision |
| **Time** | 1 course overload | 1 thesis block + 1 course overload | 1 thesis block + 1 course overload | 2 thesis blocks | 1 thesis block (1 directed study) |

Typical deliverables by quarter follow. Your specific timeline will be based on
your topic, but will likely vary only slightly.

## Quarter 4: Background

Develop a specific thesis question and investigate the research literature to
describe how your topic fits within the context of the current literature.

Mid-quarter:

- Second Draft, thesis proposal
- Outline of Literature Review chapter

End of quarter:

- Final Draft, thesis proposal, including specific anticipated contributions
- First Draft, Literature Review chapter, with document database and automated
  cross-references
- Detailed Outline of Introduction

## Quarter 3: Foundation

Acquire the knowledge and skills required to execute your approach. This may
include reproducing previous results from the literature, learning new tools, or
setting up new systems — vehicles, sensors, and so on.

Beginning of quarter:

- Full Outline of Approach chapter

Mid-quarter:

- First Draft of Introduction and Approach chapters

End of quarter:

- Second Draft of Introduction and Approach chapters

## Quarter 2: Execution

The culmination of the previous two quarters, and where the "doing" of the thesis
work happens. By the end of the quarter you should have answered your thesis
question.

Beginning of quarter:

- Full Outline of Results and Analysis chapter

End of quarter:

- 90% of thesis research complete
- Detailed Outline of Results and Analysis chapter

## Quarter 1: Documentation

The emphasis shifts from doing the research to documenting the results. You begin
by drafting the Results and Analysis chapter; assembling that material usually
reveals additional work — experiments, simulations — needed to finalize the
results. This is also when you begin working with the document as a whole rather
than individual chapters.

Mid-quarter:

- First Draft of Results and Analysis chapter
- Detailed Outline of Conclusion chapter

End of quarter:

- Second Draft of Results and Analysis chapter
- First Draft of Conclusion chapter and Abstract
- First Draft of complete thesis

## Quarter 0: Graduation

This quarter guides your thesis through the revision and acceptance process.

| Week | Milestone |
|---|---|
| 2 | Submit first three chapters to thesis processing |
| **3** | **Submit Second Draft of complete thesis to your advisor** |
| 6 | Submit Third Draft to second reader |
| 8 | Submit Final Draft to the department (Chair and Program Officer) |
| 9 | Submission to thesis processing |
| 11 | Graduation |

: {tbl-colwidths="[12,88]"}

See [Working with me](working-with-me.qmd) for what the draft stages mean and how
my review fits into this schedule, and the [MAE final draft
process](../thesis-prep/final-draft-process.qmd) for the mechanics of the last
few weeks.
